items.summary: We consider the inverse problem of determining a potential for the stationary Schrödinger equation on certain Riemannian manifolds with boundary from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We derive two unique identifiability results. The first assumes that the Riemannian metric is close to the Euclidean metric, with the closeness quantified by a relative Fourier condition imposed on the potential function. The second assumes that the manifold is of product type and that the potential function is additively separable. Both the results and the technical arguments are new, contributing to the advancement of this challenging open inverse problem.
items.title: Determining Schrodinger Potentials on Riemannian Manifolds

items.summary: LLM-based agents generate and execute multi-step plans that invoke external tools which can access private data or execute commands. In this setting, security is a property of the entire execution that a plan creates, not just any single step. The plan itself is a critical artefact that captures the tool calls, control flow, and data dependencies. We present CaMeLoT, a complement to CaMeL, an existing defence against prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. CaMeLoT extends CaMeL by adding a static verification layer that checks an agent's plan before any tool is invoked. CaMeLoT translates a generated plan into a finite-state transition system, labels it with tool calls, provenance and taint information, and checks it against temporal policies expressed in CTL using the nuXmv model checker. Because verification happens before execution, unsafe plans are rejected without using LLM calls or tool calls, saving tokens that runtime could have cost, as well as the need to unwind changes or teardown temporary sandboxes. When a verification fails, the model checker returns a counterexample to give feedback to the agent to repair the plan. We evaluate CaMeLoT on policies derived from the AgentDojo benchmark, SOC workflows, and prompt-extraction experiments, showing that it verifies a broad class of temporal properties before execution while preserving CaMeL's runtime-checkable coverage.
items.title: CaMeLoT: CaMeL orchestrated with Temporal logic for static verification and liveness

items.summary: Derived data and analysis artifacts accompanying Structural memory links experimental discovery and computational novelty . Author note: D. Nguyen and K. Cao contributed equally to this work. The analysis embeds 167,392 ICSD entries with CrystalWeave, follows structural neighborhoods through publication time, and compares public cohorts from GNoME, MatterGen, Materials Project theoretical-only, JARVIS-DFT and Alexandria-PBE. Alternative representations are Magpie-22, Graphlet (CrystalNN), Graphlet (VoronoiNN), and AMD-100. The artifacts cover historical densification and research renaissances, external-cohort basin occupancy, scale-invariant formula precedent, and synthesis-outcome comparisons using A-Lab and the Kononova collection. Corrections: Feature-dependent analyses were regenerated after corrections to elemental-species and disordered-site handling, periodic neighbors and graph construction, Graphlet encoding, and AMD basin eligibility. Candidate-structure figures preserve the source fractional coordinates and distinguish candidate symmetry from community statistics. Earlier feature matrices, assignments and numerical results must not be mixed with this release. Files: Sixteen individually downloadable files: four compressed feature archives, a derived-analysis archive split into eight numbered parts, an exact public-repository source snapshot, README, release manifest and SHA-256 checksums. Join the eight analysis parts as described in the README before extraction. The archives use tar plus Zstandard compression (.tar.zst). The analysis archive includes AMD-100 features, fitted projection states, assignments, numerical controls, corrected candidate figures, and the 57 public pre-experiment A-Lab targets with provenance. Its current-results guide identifies superseded AMD and Magpie diagnostics. Raw Magpie-22 descriptors (~6 GB) are omitted; partition PCA coordinates, current common-transform scoring coordinates and fitted state are supplied. Recomputing analyses that read those inputs requires an appropriate ICSD license. Selected external structures retain their documented public-source provenance. The release manifest records the source commit and archive checksums. Dataset license: CC BY 4.0; source code and third-party components retain their accompanying license notices.

items.summary: We examine the inverse problem of recovering the potential term of an n-dimensional heat equation from a single time solution profile. We show that it is possible to uniquely determine this potential term via a stability inequality using solution measurements taken at a fixed time, assuming the potential is known within an arbitrary subdomain. The approach is based on the Carleman estimate. Additionally, we discuss the optimality of this type of observation.
items.title: Inverse problems for the diffusion equation with one time observation

items.summary: Phase-field trajectories governed by the Allen--Cahn equation determine the effective force $G=F'/\eps^2$, but not the free-energy potential $F$ and interfacial scale $\eps$ separately. We introduce surface-tension-calibrated Allen--Cahn identification (STAC), a two-step method that resolves this ambiguity using an independently supplied surface tension. First, space--time weak moments produce a linear inverse problem without differentiating the measured field. A Bernstein representation with positive coefficients enforces two stable pure phases and a single central energy maximum. Second, the surface tension fixes the remaining scale algebraically. We prove scale equivalence of the forward model, uniqueness of the calibrated pair within this class, and finite perturbation bounds that remain valid when the potential vanishes at the pure phases. Experiments with resolved synthetic phase fields separate the effects of the structural constraint, ridge regularization, and constitutive approximation error. Across 80 shared noisy records, unconstrained degree-five regression produces six potentials with an incorrect well structure. Positivity combined with ridge regularization eliminates these violations and reduces the mean force error from 8.70\% to 5.66\%. Lower-degree models are nevertheless more accurate in some tests, and an admissible law outside the positive Bernstein family shows how the constraint can introduce approximation bias. STAC thus recovers a structurally admissible, physically scaled potential while making explicit which information comes from the observed dynamics and which comes from the independent surface-tension datum.
items.title: Constrained weak identification of Allen--Cahn free energies with surface-tension calibration

items.summary: Long-range infrared imaging frequently confronts dense target clusters whose diffraction-limited signatures merge into a single indistinguishable blob, concealing the number, sub-pixel positions, and radiant intensities of the underlying sources. While deep learning has advanced general object detection, resolving such Closely-Spaced Infrared Small Targets (CSIST) remains largely unexplored, owing to a systemic infrastructure void and a fundamental paradigm mismatch. The dominant formulation, which reduces unmixing to a blind, discrete sub-pixel separation, is inherently insufficient: without semantic guidance, the ill-posed inverse problem admits ambiguous solutions plagued by false and missed detections, while grid-based discretization locks predictions onto fixed lattice centers, chaining precision to prohibitively expensive grid refinement. We argue that CSIST unmixing should instead be informed and continuous. To ground this paradigm shift, we establish the first comprehensive open-source ecosystem for the field, comprising the large-scale CSIST-100K benchmark, a tailored metric suite, and the GrokCSO toolkit. Upon this foundation, we propose DISTA-Net++, which anchors a dynamic deep unfolding backbone with two synergistic mechanisms: a Count-Guided Prior that injects the global target count as an explicit semantic constraint to regularize the solution space, and a Continuous Coordinate Rectification that regresses off-grid offsets to decouple localization accuracy from grid resolution. Extensive experiments validate our paradigm: even under the most economical 3x division, DISTA-Net++ surpasses 7x-division state-of-the-art methods by 16.15% in CSO-mAP and 62.96% in count accuracy at merely one-sixth of their computation, demonstrating that unmixing precision need not be purchased with finer discretization. The complete ecosystem is available at https://github.com/GrokCV/GrokDet.
items.title: DISTA-Net++: Rethinking Infrared Small Target Unmixing Beyond Sub-Pixel Separation

items.summary: We present a physics-informed machine learning framework based on Neural Ordinary Differential Equations that solves the holographic inverse problem: reconstructing the bulk spacetime and gauge field of a charged AdS black hole directly from boundary fermionic spectral functions. Encoding the UV asymptotics, horizon regularity, and zero temperature extremality as hard constraints in the neural network architecture, our framework reliably reconstructs the extremal Reissner-Nordström AdS geometry across three quantum critical regimes set by the $U(1)$ probe charge---non-Fermi liquid, marginal Fermi liquid (strange metal), and Fermi-liquid-like states---and can jointly infer the probe charge itself to sub-percent accuracy. Relaxing the near-AdS boundary constraint uncovers a geometrical degeneracy: bulk profiles that differ throughout the radial direction but share the same near-horizon $AdS_2 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ data reproduce identical spectral functions near the Fermi surface. This isospectral non-uniqueness is precisely the bulk degeneracy expected on general holographic grounds at zero temperature, and its spontaneous emergence across independent training runs shows that the network isolates the IR CFT universality rather than overfitting a single UV completion.
items.title: Deep learning emergent spacetime from fermionic spectral functions in holography

items.summary: Analysis code, derived result tables, figures and the pre-specified analysis plan for a study of direction-consistent differential gene expression between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (GSE89632, GSE126848) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA). Contains the complete pipeline in Python, the output and provenance record of every stage, the full direction-consistent gene table and enrichment table untruncated, and the analysis plan with its thresholds fixed before any data were examined together with the amendments made afterwards. Raw input data is not included: all three datasets are public and are better obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCI Genomic Data Commons. The provenance files record exactly which files were retrieved, when, and with what checksums. The five folders are uploaded as one zip archive each because the repository accepts at most 100 files per record. README.md and MANIFEST.tsv are left unpacked.
items.title: NAFLD and bladder urothelial carcinoma transcriptome overlap: analysis code and derived results

items.summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. The suite carries eight corpora: the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, an artifact-binding contract, a cross-run record contract, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. This deposit covers suite revision 28 of the corpus: 272 vectors, of which 61 accept, 209 reject and 2 are indeterminate, exercised by rails in two languages. The bytes are fixed by the corpus digest 8b035678def9e5ac00ba761b8c640e4412c57163134afb9d2c1a90f49d573a52 recorded in vectors/MANIFEST.json, which tells this deposit from any other revision without anyone recounting it. The corpus is versioned and immutable per revision. A published revision is never mutated in place; a normative change to the predicate, or an addition to the corpus, bumps the revision and regenerates every vector byte-identically from its generators, because the vendored specification's digest is itself a corpus input. The intended use is citation by a conformance requirement. A requirement that names this suite, or any other suite demonstrated to exercise the same conditions, is checkable by a party who trusts neither the producer nor the implementer.
items.title: agent-evidence-vectors: conformance vectors for agent execution evidence

items.summary: Unified quality-controlled airborne HR-AMS observations (30,710 60-s records from five NASA campaigns) and surface OA factor time series (2.5 million records from European, Chinese and literature-compiled sites), assembled for a global re-examination of organic aerosol aging frameworks. Includes full provenance registry.
items.title: GlobalOA-DB v1.0: A Unified Quality-Controlled Organic Aerosol Oxidation-State and Factor Dataset

items.summary: Traditional blockchain-based document notarization follows a snapshot-oriented model in which each document revision is represented as an independent state anchored on-chain through a cryptographic reference. While effective for immutable artifacts, this approach becomes inadequate when documents evolve through collaborative editing. Concurrent modifications create divergent document versions that must be reconciled outside the notarization layer, while even minor changes require generating and distributing new document snapshots. Conversely, collaborative replication frameworks such as CRDTs provide deterministic reconciliation of concurrent updates, but do not inherently provide independently verifiable evidence of when contributions were published. This paper introduces Fluid Notarization, a notarization paradigm in which document evolution itself becomes the object of notarization. Rather than certifying isolated states, Fluid Notarization certifies a graph of causally related evolution artifacts generated by a JSON-native delta-CRDT. The proposed model builds upon Melda, which represents document changes as compact, content-addressed deltas linked through causal dependencies. Blockchain notarization is reduced to recording identifiers of these evolution artifacts, while synchronization, reconstruction, and conflict resolution remain entirely off-chain. The resulting architecture combines two complementary guarantees: deterministic convergence provided by the CRDT and independently auditable proof-of-existence, provenance, and publication evidence provided by the blockchain. A prototype implementation and validation scenario based on collaboratively edited electronic health records demonstrate the feasibility of the approach and highlight the advantages of notarizing document evolution rather than successive document snapshots.
items.title: Fluid Notarization: Verifiable Evolution of Concurrently Edited Structured Documents

items.summary: Supplementary data and code accompanying the manuscript “An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach” (Humanities and Social Sciences Communications; Manuscript ID eaed1ecb-153b-4b2f-99cf-8bca05b564b3). This package provides materials for editors and referees to check the study’s methods and results. It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. The study synthesizes published historical sources, museum catalogues, and publicly disclosed institutional records. No new laboratory, survey, or interview datasets were generated. Author-generated materials are shared under CC BY 4.0; copyrighted verbatim text of published sources is cited but not reproduced in full. Natural Earth data are public domain.
items.title: Supplementary for "An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach"

items.summary: Multimodal coding agents are expected to turn visual inputs into usable artifacts, and they act through a harness, the layer of tools, context management, and execution environment around the model. Existing evaluations often isolate short tool calls, API traces, or screenshot resemblance, and a low score under these proxies cannot say whether the model saw poorly, planned poorly, or was failed by its harness. We study scientific overview figure reconstruction, an agent task in which a source image must become an editable PowerPoint slide that preserves text, topology, layout, and native document structure. We introduce ReFigBench, a benchmark and evaluation framework built on 1,000 real overview figures retrieved from arXiv papers with full provenance. Coding agents from four model families reconstruct every figure under two workflows, direct code generation and a specialized PPTX workflow, and the strongest model runs inside two commercial harnesses, yielding ten configurations. Evaluation combines deterministic artifact checks, repeated automated scoring by judges from two model families, and blinded human comparisons. Perception remains a bottleneck that iterative rendering only partly repays. Whether workflow effort converts into quality depends on the model together with its harness, since the same model gains from the specialized workflow inside one harness and loses inside the other, and the harness shifts scores even under an identical direct prompt. The specialized workflow erases native connectors in every configuration, human judges still prefer its renderings in most matchups, and even the strongest agent falls short of the rubric ceiling. These results expose the tension between fidelity and editability as the central challenge for practical multimodal document agents.
items.title: ReFigBench: Benchmarking Scientific Figure Reconstruction as Editable PowerPoint Artifacts

items.summary: This dataset contains 93 manually selected RELION 2D class averages generated from particle images in the EMPIAR-12036 entry of the Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive. The underlying molecule has D3 symmetry. The authors initially generated a set of class averages using RELION and manually selected 93 classes after discarding those that were visually uninterpretable. Each selected image is 320 by 320 pixels. items.summary: We consider the inverse problem of determining a potential for the stationary Schrödinger equation on certain Riemannian manifolds with boundary from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We derive two unique identifiability results. The first assumes that the Riemannian metric is close to the Euclidean metric, with the closeness quantified by a relative Fourier condition imposed on the potential function. The second assumes that the manifold is of product type and that the potential function is additively separable. Both the results and the technical arguments are new, contributing to the advancement of this challenging open inverse problem.
items.title: Determining Schrodinger Potentials on Riemannian Manifolds

items.summary: Large language model agents tune GPU kernels and serving engines through a closed loop of propose, measure, and keep, but the measurements behind this loop are not trustworthy. We characterize four failure modes from a four-day pilot corpus of 619 model calls: strawman baselines manufacture speedups, absolute times do not transfer across machines, saturated tasks nullify comparisons, and infrastructure defects impersonate science. We present AutoTuneBench, a benchmark and measurement protocol that makes trust architectural. The protocol is frozen as code with test-enforced provenance; a database-level validator rejects out-of-protocol results; anti-cheat checks run outside the agent's modification surface; comparisons follow pre-registered readouts; and measurements anchor to externally published results, grounded in paired-seed statistics with a 5\% cross-run coefficient-of-variation cap. Honest measurement rewrites the headlines: our best kernel reads 10.6x against a naive baseline but 2.03x against the honest one; one configuration delivers 1.174x on one machine and 1.0049x on another; a pre-registered on/off comparison nulls at a shared wall (2.4840 vs 2.4957\,ms); and the KernelBench Level-1 suite admits 51\% of tasks with median speedup 1.0001x over PyTorch eager. The protocol, the two-engine corpus (vLLM and SGLang), and its audit trail are released as open artifacts.
items.title: AutoTuneBench: Trustworthy Measurement for Agent Auto-Tuning of LLM Serving Engines

items.summary: Analysis code, derived result tables, figures and the pre-specified analysis plan for a study of direction-consistent differential gene expression between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (GSE89632, GSE126848) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA). Contains the complete pipeline in Python, the output and provenance record of every stage, the full direction-consistent gene table and enrichment table untruncated, and the analysis plan with its thresholds fixed before any data were examined together with the amendments made afterwards. Raw input data is not included: all three datasets are public and are better obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCI Genomic Data Commons. The provenance files record exactly which files were retrieved, when, and with what checksums. The five folders are uploaded as one zip archive each because the repository accepts at most 100 files per record. README.md and MANIFEST.tsv are left unpacked.
items.title: NAFLD and bladder urothelial carcinoma transcriptome overlap: analysis code and derived results

items.summary: Agentic workflows now make consequential decisions in regulated settings, and the governance placed around them is almost entirely step-scoped: input-output classifiers, per turn rails, and span-level evaluators. The policies organizations actually hold, such as referral thresholds, authority limits, and review requirements, are properties of the whole execution rather than of any one step. This mismatch admits a failure mode we call a Compositional Policy Violation (CPV): every individual step passes its own check while the composed execution violates the governing policy. A predicate over a single step cannot evaluate a property that step does not determine, so no improvement in the accuracy of the step-scoped monitors detects this class. We define CPVs as the failure of step-level compliance to compose, and present a taxonomy of four types: Authority Creep, Threshold Laundering, Cumulative Sum Violation, and Context Collapse. We show that the correct repair for each class is dictated by where the guarded quantity mutates. We then introduce a provenance-aware runtime architecture that evaluates policies over complete execution traces, recomputing guarded quantities from raw provenance rather than the pipeline's derived representation.
items.title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails In Agentic AI Workflows

Contents Analysis backend • ProteoAnalystR_1.0.0.tar.gz — the R backend under review (source package; also at   github.com/xia-lab/ProteoAnalystR), with its build commit and SHA-256. Benchmarks (public controlled-mixture ground truth; each bundle self-contained and self-scoring) • DDA / MaxQuant — iPRG-2015 (MassIVE RMSV000000249.2; SI Table S5a): three differential-   expression engine arms (limma, DEqMS, msqrob2) scored head-to-head against the published   MSstats reference, plus the missing-value robustness sweep (Table S7) and a reproducible   DE-runtime sweep (Table S10); and a second, independent DDA spike-in on DEqMS's own MaxLFQ   two-proteome example (PRIDE PXD000279; Table S5b). • DIA / Spectronaut — LFQbench HYE124 (Table S6a): the shipped msqrob2 default vs limma and   DEqMS arms, scored against species-defined truth and the MSstats reference; and a second,   independent DIA spike-in on the UPS1 example dataset (ExperimentHub EH7782; MassIVE   MSV000087597; Table S6b). • MSstatsPTM simulations (Table S8) and the Hogrebe two-species phospho spike-in (PRIDE   PXD007145; Table S9) — protein-adjusted PTM and site-level phospho accuracy vs MSstatsPTM,   including a native MSstatsPTM package arm. • A provenance/reports bundle (fetch scripts, checksums, and   the manuscript-cited scoring report). • Two method-validation bundles: semi-synthetic PTM-occupancy / isoform-usage mixtures (Tables   S11 and S13), and an orthogonal transcript (DM1) validation of the isoform-usage detector   (Table S12). Case studies (reproduce end-to-end from the download) • CS1 palmitate islets; CS2 FB231 mitophagy; CS3 phospho / TKI resistance (PRIDE PXD005536);   CS4 isoform-usage + PTM occupancy. Each carries its inputs, bundled annotation, recorded command   history, expected results, and sessionInfo.txt. Data availability: the benchmark inputs derive from public MassIVE/PRIDE deposits; CS3 is PRIDE PXD005536; CS1 is ethics-approved, de-identified human and stem-cell-derived islet proteomics generated by the James Johnson lab (University of British Columbia); CS2 and CS4 were generated by the Jean-François Trempe lab (McGill University).

items.summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study" . This package contains everything needed to regenerate every table, figure and reported number in the manuscript from the analysis outputs, except the raw trajectories. Systems and sampling: three FGFR1 kinase domain systems (wild type, V561M, N546K) in complex with erdafitinib, three independent 500 -ns replicates each , analysed over the 200 -500 ns plateau. Nominal sampling 4.5 us; realised aggregate production sampling 4.491 us. All three systems share a 9.28387 nm cubic SPC water box with 0.15 M NaCl (total atoms 78 , 608 / 78 , 609 / 78 , 624 ). Contents: - scripts/ - 14 analysis and plotting scripts (Python 3.10 ) covering every main and supplementary figure panel - tables/ - 38 per-replicate and summary result tables (CSV) - matrices/ - 24 DCCM matrices, common-subspace PCA projections and RMSD series (NumPy .npy) - mdp/ - GROMACS run-control files (minimisation, ions, NVT, NPT, production) plus the fully expanded grompp parameter file - tpr/ - the nine production run inputs (complete, with all parameters baked in ) - topology/ - GROMACS topology files ( system and protein topologies, posre.itp, ligand parameters, index files ) - README.md - directory layout, frame-selection rules, uncertainty conventions, table/figure provenance, and full run parameters Software: GROMACS 2024.6 (production) and 2024.3 (analysis), gmx_MMPBSA 1.6 .5 , MDTraj 1.10 .3 , Python 3.10 (NumPy 2.2 .6 , SciPy 1.15 .2 , Matplotlib). Replicate-level statistics use one value per independent trajectory ( n = 3 per system ) and are reported as mean +/- SD ; frames within a trajectory are not treated as independent samples . Per-residue decomposition values are reported as mean +/- SEM , which can be converted to SD by multiplying by the square root of 3 . Important for regeneration: the production runs were executed as a 200 -ns run followed by a 300 -ns extension (gmx convert -tpr -extend). md.mdp therefore defines only the first 200 ns and must be read together with that extension step. See README.md section 7. Raw trajectories (approximately 13 GB, full atom resolution, 100 -ps output cadence) are available from the corresponding author on request .
items.title: Reproducibility package for: Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study

items.summary: LLM-based agents generate and execute multi-step plans that invoke external tools which can access private data or execute commands. In this setting, security is a property of the entire execution that a plan creates, not just any single step. The plan itself is a critical artefact that captures the tool calls, control flow, and data dependencies. We present CaMeLoT, a complement to CaMeL, an existing defence against prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. CaMeLoT extends CaMeL by adding a static verification layer that checks an agent's plan before any tool is invoked. CaMeLoT translates a generated plan into a finite-state transition system, labels it with tool calls, provenance and taint information, and checks it against temporal policies expressed in CTL using the nuXmv model checker. Because verification happens before execution, unsafe plans are rejected without using LLM calls or tool calls, saving tokens that runtime could have cost, as well as the need to unwind changes or teardown temporary sandboxes. When a verification fails, the model checker returns a counterexample to give feedback to the agent to repair the plan. We evaluate CaMeLoT on policies derived from the AgentDojo benchmark, SOC workflows, and prompt-extraction experiments, showing that it verifies a broad class of temporal properties before execution while preserving CaMeL's runtime-checkable coverage.
items.title: CaMeLoT: CaMeL orchestrated with Temporal logic for static verification and liveness

items.summary: Autonomous and semi-autonomous artificial intelligence systems can perform consequential work across multiple tools, repositories, services, and organizational roles. Existing governance frameworks establish valuable expectations for accountability, human oversight, risk management, logging, and provenance, but they do not collectively define an event-level control and evidence protocol for human-supervised agentic operations. This specification defines a testable profile in which a designated human supervisor retains effective operational control; every human and software actor operates under bounded authority; consequential actions pass explicit approval gates; and material events produce authenticated, append-only, independently verifiable provenance records. The profile maps organizational controls to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, ISO/IEC 38507:2022, ISO/IEC 42005:2025, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework; human oversight and logging controls to Articles 12 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; provenance semantics to W3C PROV; separation of duties to NIST SP 800-53; and cryptographic transparency to IETF RFC 9943 and RFC 9942. It also states the limits of cryptographic evidence: internal hash consistency does not establish actor identity, authorization, statement accuracy, or independent custody. HAIO-GATS is intended as a research and implementation baseline for accountable AI operations, standards development, conformity assessment, and empirical evaluation.
items.title: Human-Supervised AI Operations Governance and Audit Trail Specification: A Standards-Aligned Profile for Accountable Agentic Workflows

items.summary: This repository contains the complete synthetic dataset and reproducible code supporting the manuscript  and you need to unzip it inorder to see the files.  contents of the file include the following ;  A 2000-scenario synthetic dataset of catchment, storm, and green infrastructure (GI) typology-coverage combinations, generated from parameterized, non-linear analytical relationships (peak-flow attenuation and total-suspended-solids event-mean-concentration reduction as functions of imperviousness, storm return period, and coverage of four GI typologies: bioretention, green roofs, permeable pavement, vegetated swales). R scripts implementing the full modelling pipeline described in the manuscript: dataset generation; an 80/20 stratified train–test split; 5-fold cross-validated hyperparameter tuning; training of a linear regression baseline, a random forest model, and an XGBoost model; computation of R², RMSE, and MAE; feature-importance analysis (node-impurity for random forest, gain-based for XGBoost); and indicative runtime benchmarking. A Python implementation (scikit-learn, xgboost) used to produce the exact numbers and figures reported in the revised manuscript's Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–3, run under a fixed, documented random seed for full reproducibility. Precomputed results (model metrics, feature importances, test-set predictions) and the two main results figures as published
items.title: Machine Learning Surrogate Modelling in R for Rapid Screening of Green Infrastructure Hydrological Performance in Urban Stormwater Management: A Proof-of-Concept Study Using Synthetic Data

items.summary: SynInsight Atlas is a literature-derived synthesis pathway dataset for developing and evaluating machine-learning retrosynthesis models. It contains 6,555 reaction-step occurrences across 635 recorded paths from 91 publications , representing 2,166 distinct operations. The dataset is provided in CSV format, with molecular structures, reaction conditions, route connectivity, source references, and curation status. Field definitions, provenance records, and file checksums support reproducible reuse. This is a candidate release pending independent chemical review . Paths include partial syntheses, fragment preparations, and control branches; shared operations may occur in multiple paths. No fixed evaluation split or starting-material stock is supplied. Data and annotations are released under CC BY 4.0 . Original publications and supporting-information files are not included.
items.title: SynInsight Atlas: Literature-Derived Synthesis Pathways for Retrosynthesis Benchmarking

Benchmarks (public controlled-mixture ground truth; each bundle self-contained and self-scoring) • DDA / MaxQuant — iPRG-2015 (MassIVE RMSV000000249.2; SI Table S5a): three differential-   expression engine arms (limma, DEqMS, msqrob2) scored head-to-head against the published   MSstats reference, plus the missing-value robustness sweep (Table S7) and a reproducible   DE-runtime sweep (Table S10); and a second, independent DDA spike-in on DEqMS's own MaxLFQ   two-proteome example (PRIDE PXD000279; Table S5b). • DIA / Spectronaut — LFQbench HYE124 (Table S6a): the shipped msqrob2 default vs limma and   DEqMS arms, scored against species-defined truth and the MSstats reference; and a second,   independent DIA spike-in on the UPS1 example dataset (ExperimentHub EH7782; MassIVE   MSV000087597; Table S6b). • MSstatsPTM simulations (Table S8) and the Hogrebe two-species phospho spike-in (PRIDE   PXD007145; Table S9) — protein-adjusted PTM and site-level phospho accuracy vs MSstatsPTM,   including a native MSstatsPTM package arm. • A provenance/reports bundle (fetch scripts, checksums, and   the manuscript-cited scoring report). • Two method-validation bundles: semi-synthetic PTM-occupancy / isoform-usage mixtures (Tables   S11 and S13), and an orthogonal transcript (DM1) validation of the isoform-usage detector   (Table S12). Case studies (reproduce end-to-end from the download) • CS1 palmitate islets; CS2 FB231 mitophagy; CS3 phospho / TKI resistance (PRIDE PXD005536);   CS4 isoform-usage + PTM occupancy. Each carries its inputs, bundled annotation, recorded command   history, expected results, and sessionInfo.txt. Data availability: the benchmark inputs derive from public MassIVE/PRIDE deposits; CS3 is PRIDE PXD005536; CS1 is ethics-approved, de-identified human and stem-cell-derived islet proteomics generated by the James Johnson lab (University of British Columbia); CS2 and CS4 were generated by the Jean-François Trempe lab (McGill University).
items.title: ProteoAnalyst: benchmarks and case-study

items.summary: Agentic browsers can execute security-sensitive actions under a user's authenticated session, making indirect prompt injection and deceptive confirmation interfaces a direct threat to action integrity. Existing human-in-the-loop (HITL) safeguards are insufficient when the approval prompt itself can be influenced by untrusted page content or model-generated text. We present the \emph{Verifiable Action Card} (VAC), an architectural defence that reconstructs approval information from the ground-truth pending browser action and trusted intent provenance, renders it out-of-band in the trusted browser chrome, and binds approval to the exact action re-verified at dispatch. VAC combines provenance fencing, a ground-truth action descriptor, default-deny confirmation, provenance-aware risk gating, and execution binding. We implement VAC in a complete agentic browser and evaluate it on a 24-scenario benchmark covering confused-deputy attacks, Lies-in-the-Loop dialog forging, indirect prompt injection, adaptive action substitution, provenance evasion, and legitimate tasks. Across the evaluated LLMs, attack success without VAC ranges from $68\%$ to $100\%$, whereas VAC reduces attack success to $0\%$ on every model, with $78\%$ legitimate-task completion and a $0\%$ false-block rate. These results show that grounding approval in the action that will actually execute provides architectural protection against security failures that prompt-level defences and conventional HITL confirmation cannot reliably prevent.
items.title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents

items.summary: LLM-based agents generate and execute multi-step plans that invoke external tools which can access private data or execute commands. In this setting, security is a property of the entire execution that a plan creates, not just any single step. The plan itself is a critical artefact that captures the tool calls, control flow, and data dependencies. We present CaMeLoT, a complement to CaMeL, an existing defence against prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. CaMeLoT extends CaMeL by adding a static verification layer that checks an agent's plan before any tool is invoked. CaMeLoT translates a generated plan into a finite-state transition system, labels it with tool calls, provenance and taint information, and checks it against temporal policies expressed in CTL using the nuXmv model checker. Because verification happens before execution, unsafe plans are rejected without using LLM calls or tool calls, saving tokens that runtime could have cost, as well as the need to unwind changes or teardown temporary sandboxes. When a verification fails, the model checker returns a counterexample to give feedback to the agent to repair the plan. We evaluate CaMeLoT on policies derived from the AgentDojo benchmark, SOC workflows, and prompt-extraction experiments, showing that it verifies a broad class of temporal properties before execution while preserving CaMeL's runtime-checkable coverage.
items.title: CaMeLoT: CaMeL orchestrated with Temporal logic for static verification and liveness
